Nina (CS): Heads-up: Lena from StartupOps is stuck on onboarding. Their CI warmup is spiking preflight 429s and they worry about hitting rate limits before launch + renewal in 5 weeks.
Lena (StartupOps): We run 200 parallel containers during rollout. Each does a quick SDK init and an embed call. We see bursts of 429s and a bunch of short-lived tokens.
Ravi (Eng): Can you share the init call and roughly peak QPS?
Lena (StartupOps): Peak ~850 qps over ~25s. Init snippet: ```python
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'], prefetch=True)
client.embed('startup')
```
Nina (CS): Logs show `preflight_quota_exceeded` and token_age sometimes <2s.
Ravi (Eng): Likely a fanout + token churn + no keepalive. Quick fixes: reduce parallelism, add randomized splay before init, enable keepalive/connection pooling, set preflight cache window. Also we can temporarily raise their preflight burst threshold on account id so retries clear. Need acct id to proceed.
Lena (StartupOps): Account id: so-9921. We can change CI but prefer ops guidance first. How much should we reduce parallelism?
Ravi (Eng): Try groups of 10 in parallel (so 20 hosts x 10 in parallel) with 0-300ms jitter before init. In SDK set `max_concurrency` to 8 and `prefetch=false` for warmup flow. Add exponential backoff on 429 with jitter and honor Retry-After.
SDK Bot: telemetry: so-9921 preflight_429=176 at 2026-02-02T12:17:03Z, avg_preflight_latency=55ms, token_rotate=1.2/s
Lena (StartupOps): Implemented group-of-10 change + jitter. Re-ran warmup: 429s dropped to 6 over same window. Great.
Support (Ops): Created support ticket TKT-20902 to apply a temporary preflight burst increase for so-9921 during onboarding.
Nina (CS): I'll schedule a 30m enablement to walk through the runbook and send the quickstart snippet. Marking renewal team; this looked risky but now mitigated.
Lena (StartupOps): Thanks all — will follow the runbook and report back after next deployment.
